structure:
Confluence page "Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields - V4", version 210, fetched to workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/6497338582.json (tim envelope: title at .result.title, version at .result.version, storage-format HTML at .result.body, 162,599 bytes on one line). It is the data specification for the EUDP live-animal and germinal-product notification: which data a notification captures, each field's type, conditions/values, the level it applies at, its source, whether it is mandatory, an example, and which journeys it impacts. The page carries no page-level status macro (no Draft, Proposed or Superseded), so nothing on it rests on an unapproved decision; the only status macros on the page are the 70 ANIMALS and 56 GERMINALS journey markers in the Impacts column.

Layout: a short preamble (an intro paragraph, then a 'note' panel macro: 'All fields apply to both the animal and germinal journeys. Any field that applies to only one is marked as such. Where a field applies to both but the permitted values differ, the values are listed by journey.'), then 7 headed sections, each holding exactly one table — 7 tables, 94 rows in all (7 header rows, 3 full-width 'Field Block' banner rows, 84 data rows), and 13 collapsed 'expand' macros nested inside table cells:

1. h2 'Live Animal Data Elements' (bytes 750-82,452; ~81.7 KB, half the page). Preceded by a note on what 'Applies at' means and the three levels (Level 1 Notification, Level 2 Commodity line, Level 3 Unit record). Table of 8 columns — Field Name | Type | Conditions / Values | Applies at: | Source | Mandatory | Example | Impacts — with 31 field rows, each anchored: reference_number, responsible_person_for_load, country_of_origin, region_of_origin_code_requirement, region_of_origin_code, internal_reference_number, commodity_selection, type_selection, species_selection, number_of_packages, number_of_animals_quantity, animals_certified_for, contains_unweaned_animals, place_of_origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place_of_destination, permanent_address, transporter_type, commercial_transporter, private_transporter, county_parish_holding_cph, port_of_entry, arrival_date_at_port, means_of_transport, transport_identification, transport_document_reference, transited_countries, and two rows both labelled 'Contact Address' sharing the one anchor contact_address (the first sourced from gov.identity, the second user-created via the Standard address block). Holds 4 expands: 'Number of packages commodities (54)' (54 entries, title agrees), 'Contains Unweaned Animals' (5 entries, untitled count), 'Permanent address required commodities (3)' (3 entries, agrees), 'CPH required commodities (19)' (19 entries, agrees).
2. h1 'Reason of Import' (82,452-102,284; ~19.8 KB). Same 8 columns. One banner row 'Reason of Import | Field Block - Mandatory to Submit - At least one', then 19 data rows making up 5 fields: reason_for_import (enum, 5 value rows), purpose_in_internal_market (enum, 11 value rows), Destination country, Port of exit, Exit date. Each enum value row carries its own ANIMALS and/or GERMINALS markers, so a value can apply to one journey only.
3. h1 'Animal Identifiers' (102,284-119,210; ~16.9 KB). Same 8 columns. Banner row 'Animal Identifiers | Field Block - ...', then 6 field rows: animal_identifier_passport, animal_identifier_tattoo, animal_identifier_ear_tag, Horse Name (unanchored), animal_identifier_identification_details, animal_identifier_description. Holds 4 expands: 'Passport identifier commodities (6)' (9 entries — title and list disagree), 'Tattoo identifier commodities (2)' (5 entries — title and list disagree), 'Ear tag identifier commodities (4)' (4 entries, agrees), 'Horse Name' (1 entry).
4. h1 'Documents' (119,210-132,645; ~13.4 KB). Same 8 columns. Banner row 'Accompanying Document | Field Block - ...', then 4 field rows: accompanying_document_type (13 permitted values listed in-cell), accompanying_document_attachment_type, accompanying_document_reference, accompanying_document_date_of_issue.
5. h2 'Germinal Data Elements' (132,645-144,805; ~12.2 KB). 8 columns. 6 field rows: Quantity (unit/pieces), Temperature, Donor name/ID, Collection date, Production date, Identification Number/Mark. Five of the six (all but Quantity) carry an 'Applicable to' expand listing the same 12 germinal commodity entries, written with a leading zero dropped ('5111000 - Semen - Cattle', '5119985 - ...'). Closes with 'Not required for germinal products: County Parish Holding (CPH) and Permanent Address. These apply to the animal journey only.'
6. h1 'Address Block' (anchor address_block; 144,805-156,377; ~11.6 KB). The reusable Standard Address Block referenced by every party and transporter field above. 5 columns — Field Name | Attributes | Validation | Example | Impacts — and 10 field rows: Name or Organisation name, Transporter authorisation number, Address Line 1, Address Line 2, Town or city, County, Postal or Zip code, Country, Telephone number, Email address.
7. h2 'Change Log' (156,377-162,599; ~6.2 KB). 3 columns — Field Name | Notes | Date — and 8 rows. Six record a de-scoping (Arrival time at port, Journey Log, Transport after BCP, Animal Identifier - Wing Ring, all 'de-scoped by' with dates 2026-05-14/2026-05-29; Approved Establishment - germinals and Package type - germinals, 2026-09-07); two record a change (Document Type list updated 2026-10-29, Country of origin updated to 'mandatory to proceed' 2026-11-02).

Scope coverage and two departures from the scope's wording, both recorded as decisions: (a) the scope names an 'Out of Scope Data Elements' section — at version 210 the page has no section by that name; the de-scoping judgements now live in the Change Log table, so that table is read as the out-of-scope record and its 'de-scoped by' rows carry the de-scoping force the scope gives them. (b) the scope calls Address Block a 'sub-section' — it is a top-level h1 section of its own, after Germinal Data Elements. The scope takes in the whole page, so nothing is left out: all 7 sections, all 84 data rows, all 3 banner rows and all 13 expands are inside the parts. The one explicit TBC on the page is in commercial_transporter's Conditions cell ('Commercial transporters are consumed from TBC list that holds the approved transporters') and belongs to part 2.
